parties.popularity_note: No competitive elections. Proxy: the WPK's share of seats in the 1998 Supreme People's Assembly election (594 of 687 = 0.865). This is a gameplay estimate, not a vote share.

factions.name: Military leadership (National Defence Commission and Korean People's Army)
factions.note: An institutional grouping, not a documented faction: the senior commanders of the Korean People's Army, whose standing rose under the military-first (Songun) policy of the late 1990s. Jo Myong-rok was First Vice Chairman of the National Defence Commission from 1998 to November 2010. Strength is a gameplay estimate.

factions.name: Party and state apparatus
factions.note: An institutional grouping, not a documented faction: senior WPK and Supreme People's Assembly officials. Kim Yong-nam and Choe Ryong-hae chaired the SPA Presidium/Standing Committee (1998-2019 and 2019-2026); Jo Yong-won is deputy chief of the WPK Secretariat. Strength is a gameplay estimate.

factions.name: Cabinet economic administrators
factions.note: An institutional grouping, not a documented faction: the premiers who ran the Cabinet and the economy. The sub-ideology reflects the Cabinet's economic-management role, not a documented reform programme. Strength is a gameplay estimate.

parties.note: Founded on 24 June 1949 (Wikipedia infobox). Leader titles changed from First Secretary (2012) to Chairman (7th Congress, 9 May 2016) to General Secretary (8th Congress, 10 January 2021). Between Kim Jong Il's death and the 4th Party Conference (11 April 2012) the top party post was not filled; Kim Jong Il was later named Eternal General Secretary. Ideology officially Juche (Kimilsungism-Kimjongilism); no Juche sub-ideology exists, so marxist_leninist is used.

parties.popularity_note: No competitive elections. Proxy: 53 of 687 SPA seats in the 1998 election (0.077); a gameplay estimate, not a vote share.
parties.note: Founded as the Korean Democratic Party; a subordinate allied party that accepts WPK leadership, so the social_democrat sub-ideology is nominal. Kim Yong-dae's chairmanship began in August 1998 (stored as the year). The chair between Pak Yong-il's death (18 September 2022) and February 2026 is not recorded; state media identified Ri Son-gwon as chairman in March 2026 and his infobox gives February 2026.

parties.note: Subordinate allied party representing followers of the Chondogyo religion; accepts WPK leadership. Ryu Mi-yong (1921-2016) chaired it, but the fetched sources give no dates; the current infobox names Ri Myong-chol as chairman, who has no Wikipedia or Wikidata entry. No religious sub-ideology fits Chondoism, so big_tent is used. The English abbreviation 'CCP' is an editorial shorthand; the infobox gives none.

name.en: Democratic Front for the Reunification of Korea

parties.popularity_note: Not a party: the popular front through which all SPA candidates were nominated. Its seats are only used in elections.json where sources give no breakdown by member party (2003 and 2019).
parties.note: Popular front led by the WPK, uniting it with the two allied parties and mass organisations; founded 25 June 1949 and dissolved 23 March 2024 (Wikipedia infobox). Modelled as a party record only so that the 2003 and 2019 SPA results, reported as a single front total, can be stored. The colour is an editorial choice, not the front's own.
